Lessons.Title: The Quadratic Formula
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: apply the quadratic formula to ax²+bx+c=0 with a≠0, compute discriminant accurately, find both signs and compare results with factoring or graphing. Independent Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 7 Lesson 16 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/16/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/16/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source introduces the general formula and evaluates its parts explicitly.

Original quadratic 2x²+3x−2=0 has a2,b3,c−2, discriminant D=b²−4ac=9−4(2)(−2)=25. Formula x=(−3±√25)/(2×2)=(-3±5)/4 yields x=1/2 or−2. Direct factoring (2x−1)(x+2)=0 gives the same roots, an independent check.

For a second equation 3x²+2x+2=0, D=2²−4×3×2=−20, so there are no real-number solutions. The formula does not manufacture a real square root of a negative discriminant. Distinguish real-number task scope from complex roots beyond the current lesson.

Student task: label coefficients including signs, calculate D and both branches without calculator precedence errors, compare to a factorization when available, and classify negative-D example. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 for coefficient extraction, discriminant and denominator, both valid roots and error/check reasoning.

KeyConcepts.Title: Quadratic formula
KeyConcepts.Definition: For real ax²+bx+c=0 with a≠0, x=(-b±√(b²−4ac))/(2a).

KeyConcepts.Title: Discriminant
KeyConcepts.Example: D25 yields two distinct real roots.

KeyConcepts.Title: Negative D
KeyConcepts.Definition: If D<0, there are no real roots.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Do not take a real sqrt of negative.

Dividing only the square-root term by2a
Taking negative discriminant as zero real root not applicable?

SummaryPoints: The quadratic formula works for every real-coefficient quadratic with a≠0, with real roots when D≥0.
Exact coefficient signs and denominator matter.
D25 produces roots1/2 and−2 in the original example.
